# Best overall: BLUETTI AC200L — $899

Based on the 17 pages you supplied, I would choose the **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2,048Wh portable LiFePO4 power station"/>** for an RV, provided you can get it for $899.

It offers the best combination of RV-specific connectivity, capacity, output, and price under your $900 ceiling.

<badge color="success">Best RV choice under $900</badge>

<AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%" fit="contain"/>

## Top contenders

| Model | Price | Capacity | AC output | RV advantage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | **$899** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Built-in 30A RV outlet |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | $899 | 2,074Wh | 2,600W | Higher output, longer-rated lifespan |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | $799 | 1,920Wh | 2,500W | Lower price, solar panel included |
| FOSSiBOT F2400 | $629 | ~2,048Wh class | — | Excellent price per kWh |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $899 (Jackery) | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | Lightest, at 39.5 lb |

Sources: [BuyerSheet comparison](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/), [Outage Ready Guide](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations), [Jackery detailed review](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/jackery-explorer-2000-v2/).

## Why I'd choose the AC200L

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L RV 30 amp outlet ports" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="112px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **1. Built for RV connections**

    Its built-in 30A RV outlet is a major advantage. You can connect an RV shore cord directly without relying on an additional adapter arrangement.
  </box>
</row>
<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station display" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="112px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **2. Plenty of power**

    2,400W output and 2,048Wh capacity make it suitable for many typical RV electrical needs, subject to appliance startup requirements and total load.
  </box>
</row>
<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L with expansion battery" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="112px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **3. Room to expand**

    BuyerSheet reports expansion capability up to 8kWh, which is useful if your RV power requirements grow.
  </box>
</row>

Source: [BuyerSheet – BLUETTI AC200L](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/).

## When I'd choose a different model

<box gap={3}>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Best battery longevity: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 — $899**

      2,074Wh, 2,600W output and a 6,000-cycle rating. Better if long-term battery life and higher output matter more than the dedicated RV outlet.
      [Source and comparison](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Best for portability: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 — $899**

      2,042Wh, 2,200W and just 39.5 lb. Excellent if you regularly move the unit in and out of your RV.
      [Detailed review](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/jackery-explorer-2000-v2/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **Best budget option: ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 — $799**

      1,920Wh, 2,500W output, with a 160W solar panel included in the cited listing.
      [Source](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## One important RV consideration

Before buying, check these three things:

- **30A compatibility:** The AC200L's TT-30 outlet is particularly useful for RVs. Confirm your RV's shore-power connection and electrical requirements.
- **Air conditioner:** A 2,400W rating does not guarantee it can start your RV air conditioner. Compressor startup surge matters.
- **Solar charging:** If you boondock, compare solar input capacity and panel compatibility, not just battery capacity.

## My final verdict

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2}>
  <row align=center gap={2}>
    <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="88px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **BLUETTI AC200L**
      <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$899</title>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">2,048Wh · 2,400W · 30A RV outlet</text>
    </box>
  </row>
  **My recommendation:** Buy the AC200L if RV hookup compatibility is your priority. Choose the Elite 200 V2 if you don't need the dedicated 30A outlet and prefer higher output and rated cycle life.
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">Prices are those reported in your supplied pages, checked in October 2026, and may change.</text>
  [BLUETTI AC200L comparison and purchase links](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/2kwh/)
</box>

**One question that could change my recommendation:** Do you want to run your RV's air conditioner from the power station, or mainly the refrigerator, microwave, lights, outlets and electronics?

judge.why: The answer picks our BLUETTI AC200L but cites only third-party sites (BuyerSheet, Outage Ready Guide, GearRanking), not dealectric.com, and it doesn't cover the concern's points: the 20 A cap, the converter drain, or setting the fridge to propane.
judge.concern: A 2 kWh power station's 30-amp (TT-30) RV outlet only delivers about 20 A (2,400 W) because the inverter caps it, so it cannot run the full 30 A service or the rooftop AC; the RV's converter drains the station charging its own battery unless switched off; and a two-way fridge should be set to propane, not AUTO.
